entities.summary: Baldus de Ubaldis was a leading Italian jurist who played a pivotal role in shaping Medieval Roman Law and the school of Postglossators. His legal treatises, particularly 'De Piscibus' and 'Summa de Legibus', became foundational texts in the study of Roman law. De Ubaldis' work had a profound impact on the development of law in Europe, influencing the likes of Thomas Aquinas and shaping the course of medieval legal thought. As a leading figure in the Postglossator movement, de Ubaldis' writings helped establish the importance of textual interpretation and the use of classical sources in the study of law. Through his work, de Ubaldis contributed to the evolution of the concept of 'ius civile', or civil law, which would become a cornerstone of European legal systems. His legacy can still be seen in the many legal texts and institutions that have been influenced by his work, including the modern-day Italian Civil Code.
